questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: What was crucial was that the country had a developed healthcare system. That the country was safe. That the location was not too expensive to reside in either. In this case the country is known to be very beautiful and the people very hospitable, which acted as clear motivation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The actual stay has been amazing however for it to have gotten topmarks the actual clinical stay should have been organized better, the mentors should have brought the students with procedures. Perhaps there should have been a doctor assigned to the student for each day or one could atleast recieve a type of schedule for what to do.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there was both powerpoints and zoom meetings which contained the information needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved assistance from Jenerja whom has been very helpful whenever there has been any problems or doubts.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: hmmm it is quite challenging if you do not get a dorm room. I stayed at Hostel tresor at their dorm. I can highly reccomend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of how far you are from the center, as most things happen there. However public transport and renting bicycles is super easy so it is usually okay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You arent "placed" anywhere. You can sign up for housing but few people get it so you are mostly on your own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy and there was always someone to answer questions quickly

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had some documents i had to fill it out and have some signatures from my university including signing up for a card etc. It was all quite simple and clear.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was both a coordinator from my university and the host university who always were available to answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesfull, i signed up for all the things needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask if there is a question, they are very nice and helpful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic program was quite nonexistent, you just showed up at the department and then it was your own responsibility to ask if you could see or do things.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There wasnt exactly a level, you just went to the department.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In som ways similar, not that the danish doctors are alot better at taking students with them for procedures but in denmark there is more teaching incorporated.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical courses in Anaesthesiology, Internal Medicine (Cardiology, and Hematology), Surgery (Thoracic surgery and Cardiovascular surgery)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely reccoment the surgical courses because you get to see so much of the procedure, and it is very interesting to see as a student.

questions.answer: My phonescreen broke oops

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are the same price as in denmark however going out for food, coffee, beer etc at cafes and restaurants are significantly cheaper. Especially food when you use boni.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really make use of it, although I am sure they were good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports clubs, language clubs and others

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I reccomend people show up for the ESN arranged events to meet other people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lake bled, Vellika plenina, Trieste in italy, go to see the Soca valley and Bovec and Bohinj.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people here are very kind and it is easy to fit in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, did not meet many

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The doctors at the hospital are quite "blunt/direct", which would be considere rude in denmark. However the patients seemed fine about it

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their love of nature and outdoors activities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember you have to make alot of initiative coming as a foreigner. Remember to enjoy your time off. Try to meet as many people you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find a place in the center, it is alot more fun to be central to things and try to find a place with roomates.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and experiencing a new cultures. However seeing a different hospital system and how they operate was also very interesting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to show up the clinical rotations and not having any doctors make a plan for you or anything so you sort of had to find things to do on your own.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
